- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 3–7 days.
- If history shows strong upward trend with no sentiment signal (e.g., all 0.00), model overreacts; apply mean reversion bias: cap forecast at 10–15% below recent peak.
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., 1.00 or >0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 3–7 days, especially if recent price is falling.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–5% in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias of 2–3% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often fails to recognize trend reversal; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.
